title: Set up repository structure and README
body: Create docs/ src/ tests/ notebooks/ data/ results/ with a README in each. README.md is the Start Here document. Acceptance: a new reader can find the plan, the code and the results from the front page.

title: Write scope statement and MoSCoW requirements
body: One page of scope plus a prioritised requirements list. Acceptance: both committed to docs/01-planning and approved at supervision.

title: Draft and submit the ethics form
body: Low-risk secondary data submission. Acceptance: submitted by 28 October, two days before the 30 October deadline, confirmation filed in docs/04-ethics.

title: Implement dataset loaders with a canonical schema
body: Every corpus loads as text / label / source. Acceptance: both corpora load, tests cover the schema and the missing-file error.

title: Record dataset provenance and checksums instead of committing data
body: Large file push was rejected; Git LFS evaluated and rejected. Acceptance: data/README.md records source, licence and SHA-256 for each file, and frd.download reproduces the directory.

title: Produce descriptive statistics for both corpora
body: Label balance, review length, vocabulary size. Acceptance: table in D1 section 6.

title: Complete the reading list in literature.md
body: Thirteen papers with citation, venue, dataset, method, reported score and a critique. Acceptance: synthesis table complete.

title: Draft the literature review
body: 1200 words first pass. Acceptance: committed to docs/02-research.

title: Restructure the literature review thematically
body: Feedback 15 Oct: too descriptive, paper by paper. Acceptance: three themes plus the synthesis table, ~2400 words.

title: Build the preprocessing pipeline
body: Cleaning, deduplication, stratified 70/15/15 split at a fixed seed. Acceptance: one command regenerates every split; determinism covered by a test.

title: TF-IDF + Logistic Regression baseline
body: Hypothesis: within-dataset macro-F1 above 0.85 on the crowdsourced corpus. NOTE: vectoriser must be fitted inside the CV fold. Acceptance: a row in results.csv.

title: Linear SVM baseline
body: Same protocol as #14. Acceptance: a row in results.csv.

title: Random Forest baseline
body: Same protocol as #14. Acceptance: a row in results.csv.

title: Switch reporting to macro-F1 with per-class metrics
body: Supervisor 29 Oct: accuracy is the wrong headline on a not-quite-balanced split. Acceptance: every row carries macro-F1, per-class precision and recall, confusion matrix, commit hash and seed.

title: Fine-tune distilroberta-base on a free GPU service
body: roberta-base would not load on the laptop. Acceptance: a completed run, notebook committed, checkpointing on.

title: Test SMOTE oversampling on TF-IDF features
body: Hypothesis: oversampling improves recall on the minority class. RESULT: negative, macro-F1 0.88 to 0.84. Not used; reported in the methodology.

title: Storyboard the D2 feasibility video
body: Three things to prove: data in hand, pipeline runs, Semester 2 achievable. Acceptance: storyboard committed and approved at supervision.

title: Record the D2 video
body: Screen capture plus voice-over from the script. Acceptance: recorded by 20 November.

title: Edit and check the D2 video
body: Audio levels, legibility, argument survives without the speaker. Acceptance: watched through end to end before submission.

title: Request YelpChi dataset access
body: BLOCKED pending response. Descoped to Semester 2 on 20 November; Amazon Reviews 2023 is the fallback.

title: Cross-dataset test: train crowdsourced, test machine-generated
body: Hypothesis: performance drops. RESULT: 0.88 to 0.61 macro-F1. This is the finding the project turns on.

title: Cross-dataset test: the reverse direction
body: Acceptance: rows in results.csv for both directions.

title: Combined-training condition
body: Does pooling the corpora close the gap? Acceptance: rows for each held-out test split.

title: Add character n-gram features
body: Hypothesis: char n-grams survive distribution shift better than word n-grams. Acceptance: both vectorisers in every condition.

title: Script all figure generation
body: No hand-edited charts. Acceptance: make figures regenerates every figure from results.csv.

title: Command-line predictor
body: train / predict / info. Acceptance: trains, saves, reloads and classifies a pasted review.

title: Test suite
body: Acceptance: tests cover preprocessing, datasets, models, metrics and the CLI, and run with no network access.

title: GitHub Actions CI
body: Two early runs failed: the workflow tried to load git-ignored data. Acceptance: green on main using committed fixtures, badge in the README.

title: Issue templates for experiments and writing
body: Makes the issue history usable as an experiment log. Acceptance: both templates in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE.

title: Proofread D1 against the rubric
body: Acceptance: checked against the handbook checklist and the marking rubric.

title: Final check of the D2 video
body: Acceptance: full watch-through, audio and legibility confirmed.

title: Requirements and design sections of D1
body: MoSCoW table plus traceability matrix; UML component diagram. Acceptance: committed to docs.

title: Assemble the full D1 draft for the supervisor
body: Internal deadline 12 November, two weeks before the real one. Acceptance: sent by email.

title: Revise D1 after supervisor feedback
body: Tighten the introduction, add explicit limitations, move two tables to an appendix, date the Semester 2 plan.

title: Verify reproduction from a clean clone
body: Acceptance: clone on a second machine, follow the README line by line, results reproduce.

title: Submit D1 and D2
body: Acceptance: both uploaded to Canvas by 24 November, ahead of the 26 November deadline.

title: Cut release v0.2.0-feasibility
body: Acceptance: tagged after #38 passes, release notes list every issue closed under M3 and M4.

title: Export the issue list as D4 evidence
body: gh issue list --state all --json, plus the milestone burndown and a board screenshot. Acceptance: committed to docs/06-meetings.

title: SHAP explanations of model decisions
body: Moved from Semester 1 on 5 November: a feasibility study does not need it.

title: McNemar significance testing between model pairs
body: Dietterich (1998). Moved from Semester 1 with #44.

title: Add a third corpus as a robustness check
body: Amazon Reviews 2023. Tests whether the gap holds beyond one pair.

title: Feature ablation across the four feature groups
body: Which group carries the performance, and does that change under shift?

title: Draft the ethics amendment for the user evaluation
body: Participant information sheet, consent form, data handling. Acceptance: submitted in Week 1 of Semester 2 (risk R6).

title: Build the demonstrator from the spike branch
body: Promote spike/streamlit to a proper feature branch with tests and CI. Scheduled first because it carries the ethics dependency.

title: Generate a second machine-generated review set
body: A different generator, so the generalisation claim is tested across generators and not only across corpora.
